content: A few other OSS projects I'm in have a regular weekly office hours/help desk/co-working/AMA meeting which is helpful to new contributors. This seems in particular useful when there are topics to discuss that appear still too early for an issue, let alone a PR. Is there something like this for Physlib? I'd probably call in :) maybe to get some discussion on the Feynman diagram API. (And "lean coffee" as a meeting format could be appropriate beyond the name.)

About once every couple of months we do Physlib cafe's but they are not to some regular schedule: #Physlib > The PhysLean café , but rather just 'as-and-when'. We could probably organize one for soon, and if there is appetite for something regular we could also organize that :).

I’d also be very interested in this. One hard part as a new contributor is orienting myself inside a file or topic well enough to know what small contribution would actually fit the project direction.

This seems especially useful for ideas that are too early for an issue or PR, where maintainers could give roadmap level guidance, point to references, and help keep work aligned with the broader PhysLib design.

If the larger community is interested, maybe sessions could have a fixed cadence, say once every two weeks, but proceed poll based. The host could set whatever attendance threshold makes the time worthwhile, if enough people sign up, the cafe happens, otherwise the questions can be delegated to focused Zulip threads as they are now.
I'd be happy with this! If someone would be willing to take the lead on this, I would be very grateful. (Also generally happy to answer questions about design etc. on here as well).

I'd be happy to organize the logistics, as long as no one then mistakes this for expertise :-D What is the time zone reach to target for a first iteration? Should we aim for a 2pm UTC for optimal coverage? (7am San Francisco, 11pm Tokyo)
So next: the day-of-week choice. What about starting on Wednesday July 1, 2pm GMT (google calendar apparently doesn't support a UTC timezone)?

2026-07-01T14:00:00+01:00
zulip has a built in global time that let's everyone sees it in local time :)
For me this would normally work, but this specific Wednesday it wouldn't :( - would be free any other day. But this should not stop people meeting on Wednesday.
Let's go with Thursday then. If that works, we can announce in the #Physlib > The PhysLean café thread. As done there before, I will post a zoom link an hour or two in advance.
